chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Aban ibn Taghlib said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who manumitted his female slave conditionally (tabeer), then married her to another man, and she bore children from him. Then her husband died and left children from her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her children are like her status; so when the one who manumitted her dies, they become free.'
I said to him: 'Is it permissible for the one who manumitted her mother to return her to conditional manumption if he needs to?' He said: 'Yes.'

I said: 'What if you see that if their mother dies after the husband has died, and her children from the free husband remain? Is it permissible for her master to sell her children and return them to conditional manumption?' He said: 'No. He only has the right to return her to conditional manumption if he needs to and she agrees to that.'

key_terms.تَدْبِير: Conditional manumption (a slave is freed upon the owner's death)
key_terms.يَرُدَّهَا: To return her (to the state of conditional manumption)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the children of a conditionally manumitted slave woman who marries a free man?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the complex jurisprudence of *tadbir* (conditional manumission), establishing that children of a *umm al-walad* inherit her status, thereby ensuring their freedom upon the master's death. It further delineates the master's right to reclaim the mother into slavery only if she consents and he has need, while protecting the children from being sold separately, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the mother's agency in maintaining the family unit's emancipation.
